task.title: See a family tree
task.shortdesc: Draw the parents, partners and children of one person, and read the drawing.

prereq.p: Open a person first. shows how.

context.p: The same tree also shows beside a person's page, under a heading named . This task opens it on a page of its own, at full width.

stepresult.p: A drawing opens, with the person you chose in a box with a dark edge. Their parents are in a row above. Their partners are beside them. Their children are in a row below.

info.p: A box shows a name, how that person is related, and the years of life. For example, Wife · 1783–1821. A chip on the box counts the events of that person.

step.cmd: Read the oval between two partners.

info.p: The oval shows the year of their marriage, such as m. 1812.

step.cmd: Find the two pairs of buttons above the drawing.

info.p: Each pair has a minus button, a number and a plus button. The pair marked with an up arrow shows 3. The pair marked with a down arrow shows 1. Choose a minus or a plus to see what changes.

result.p: In words, the picture shows this. Patrick Brontë is in the box with the dark edge. His wife, Maria Branwell, is beside him. The oval between them says m. 1812. Their six children are in a row below, from Maria to Anne.
Beside the number buttons are and . takes the drawing back to the person in focus. fits the drawing to the screen. A big family may go past the edge of the screen.

You can also press the drawing itself. The app says what each press does. A person's box re-roots the chart. The round mark between partners opens family events. The box of the person in focus opens their record.

postreq.p: The same tree is the pedigree in older manuals.
